name: pane
description: One column of a two-column work area: a 56px head (title and caption at half opacity, optional action button) over a body that scrolls on its own. .ds-split lays panes side by side.

props.name: id
props.description: Prefix of the title's id, used by aria-labelledby.

props.name: caption
props.description: Caption next to the title (a count, a page count).

props.name: action
props.description: Label of the head's text button.

rationale:
Head height is spacing.9 + spacing.5 (56px), side padding spacing.6, bg.surface, one hairline under it. The title uses the "title" role (Inter SemiBold 16px) and the caption the caption role (Inter Italic 16px), both at 50% opacity as in Figma, bottom-aligned so their baselines meet, spacing.cell apart. .ds-pane__body and .ds-pane__scroll are separate so a positioned body (e.g. one a loading-veil covers) can wrap the scrolling region, while a simple pane scrolls directly under the head. The scrollbar is hidden (scrollbar-width: none); wheel, keys and touch still scroll.

Attributes: data-divider="start" on the head and body draws a hairline on the pane's left edge (the divider between two panes); data-emphasis="true" on the title shows it at full opacity; a body with the hidden attribute is hidden (tab panels).

Resizable split: any flex row with data-resizable and a .ds-split__handle between two neighbours. The handle is a 0-wide flex item on the border between them, with an 8px (spacing.3) grab area centered on the line and a 2px accent line on hover, focus and while dragging. Dragging, or ArrowLeft / ArrowRight (24px a step), resizes the target: data-resize-target="end" (default) the element after the handle, "start" the one before it. data-min-size / data-min-rest set the target's and the rest's minimum in pixels (default 320 each). The size is applied as data-resized plus --_resize-size on the target, not an inline flex, so CSS states keep priority (sidebar-list's collapsed rule beats it, and the handle beside a collapsed sidebar is hidden). data-resize-key remembers the target's share of the row in localStorage (a share, so another window width keeps the proportion; missing or failing storage just starts equal). It emits ds-split-resize and a window resize, so nested splits re-apply their stored share and paper-preview's scroll thumb updates. Not sourced from Figma: the handle and resizing; the design shows only the divider line. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: The pane is a <section>; label it with aria-labelledby pointing at the title. The head button is a real text-button. The resize handle is role="separator" aria-orientation="vertical", focusable, with aria-valuenow/min/max as the end pane's share of the split in percent; give it an aria-label naming what it resizes.
